ei.title: New Beginning Dates and Goal Motivation
ei.subject: 2022 고2 11월 모의고사

fullPassage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). Whether it was starting a new gym habit or spending less time on social media, when the date that researchers suggested was associated with a new beginning, more students wanted to begin changes right then. And more recent research by a different team found that similar benefits were achieved by showing goal seekers modified weekly calendars. When calendars depicted the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the first day of the week, people reported feeling more motivated to make immediate progress on their goals.

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was ①<u>associated</u> with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). Whether it was starting a new gym habit or spending less time on social media, when the date that researchers suggested was associated with a new beginning, more students ②<u>wanted</u> to begin changes right then. And more recent research by a different team found that similar benefits were ③<u>achieved</u> by showing goal seekers modified weekly calendars. When calendars depicted the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the first day of the week, people reported ④<u>feel</u> more motivated to make immediate progress on their goals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: feel → feeling: report + 동명사(-ing) 구문
det.analysis:
✅ ① associated — be associated with(~와 관련되다) 수동태. 적절
✅ ② wanted — 주어 more students에 수일치. 과거 맥락 적절
✅ ③ achieved — were achieved by(~에 의해 달성되었다) 수동태. 적절
❌ ④ feel — 원문은 feeling. 'report + 동명사' 구조에서 feel(원형)이 아닌 feeling(동명사) 필요 ←정답
det.tip: report + V-ing: people reported feeling(느꼈다고 보고했다). report의 목적어 자리에 동명사

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more ①<u>attractive</u> time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an ②<u>unremarkable</u> day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). Whether it was starting a new gym habit or spending less time on social media, when the date that researchers suggested was associated with a new beginning, more students wanted to begin changes right then. And more recent research by a different team found that similar benefits were achieved by ③<u>showing</u> goal seekers modified weekly calendars. When calendars ④<u>depict</u> the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the first day of the week, people reported feeling more motivated to make immediate progress on their goals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: depict → depicted: 시간 부사절(When)의 과거 시제
det.analysis:
✅ ① attractive — 비교급(more attractive) + 명사 수식. 적절
✅ ② unremarkable — 관사 an + 형용사 + 명사 unremarkable day. 적절
✅ ③ showing — 전치사 by + 동명사(showing). 적절
❌ ④ depict — 원문은 depicted. 문맥상 과거 연구 내용 설명으로 과거형 depicted 필요 ←정답
det.tip: 과거 시제 일관성: 연구 결과 서술 시 동사는 과거형(found, depicted, reported)

When calendars depicted the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the first day of the week, people reported feeling more ③<u>motivated</u> to make ④<u>immediate</u> progress on their goals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: achieving → achieved: 주어 benefits는 능동 행위자가 아닌 수동 대상
det.analysis:
✅ ① than — 비교급(more attractive than) 비교 접속사. 적절
❌ ② achieving — 원문은 achieved. 'benefits were achieved by'(혜택이 달성되었다) 수동태. benefits는 행위를 하는 주체가 아니므로 능동 achieving 불가 ←정답
✅ ③ motivated — 형용사처럼 쓰인 과거분사(feel motivated). 적절
✅ ④ immediate — 형용사가 명사 progress 수식. 적절
det.tip: 수동태: benefits were achieved by ~. 주어가 행위를 받는 대상이므로 be + p.p.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: suggesting → suggested: when절의 주어 researchers에 대한 본동사 필요
det.analysis:
❌ ① suggesting — 원문은 suggested. when절의 주어 researchers에 대한 본동사가 필요하므로 현재분사 suggesting 불가. 과거형 suggested 필요 ←정답
✅ ② achieved — were achieved by(수동태). 혜택이 달성되었다는 적절한 표현
✅ ③ depicted — 과거 연구 맥락의 과거형 동사. 적절
✅ ④ progression — '발전/진행' 의미의 명사로 문맥상 허용 가능
det.tip: 종속절(when/if절)에도 반드시 '주어 + 동사' 구조가 있어야 함. 분사 suggesting은 동사 역할 불가

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more ①<u>attractive</u> time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). Whether it was starting a new gym habit or spending less time on social media, when the date that researchers suggested was associated with a new beginning, more students wanted to ②<u>begin</u> changes right then. And more recent research by a different team found that similar benefits were ③<u>achieved</u> by showing goal seekers modified weekly calendars. When calendars depicted the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the ④<u>last</u> day of the week, people reported feeling more motivated to make immediate progress on their goals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: last(마지막) → first(첫 번째): '새로운 시작'이라는 핵심 주제에 반하는 단어
det.analysis:
✅ ① attractive(매력적인): 새로운 시작과 연관된 날짜를 더 매력적으로 본다는 맥락 적절
✅ ② begin(시작하다): 더 많은 학생들이 즉시 변화를 시작하길 원했다는 맥락 적절
✅ ③ achieved(달성된): 유사한 혜택이 달성되었다는 맥락 적절
❌ ④ last(마지막): 원문은 first. 달력이 현재 날을 '첫 번째' 날로 묘사해야 새로운 시작 효과가 생김 ←정답
det.tip: first day of the week(한 주의 첫날) = 새로운 시작 = 동기 부여. last(마지막)로 바꾸면 의미 정반대

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more attractive time to ①<u>kick-start</u> goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). Whether it was starting a new gym habit or spending ②<u>less</u> time on social media, when the date that researchers suggested was associated with a new beginning, more students wanted to begin changes right then. And more recent research by a different team found that ③<u>similar</u> benefits were achieved by showing goal seekers modified weekly calendars. When calendars depicted the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the first day of the week, people reported feeling more ④<u>discouraged</u> to make immediate progress on their goals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: discouraged(의욕이 꺾인) → motivated(동기부여된): 새로운 시작 날짜는 동기를 높임
det.analysis:
✅ ① kick-start(시작하다/활성화하다): 목표 추구를 시작하는 맥락 적절
✅ ② less(더 적은): 소셜미디어에 더 적은 시간을 쓰기 시작한다는 맥락 적절
✅ ③ similar(유사한): 비슷한 혜택이 달성되었다는 맥락 적절
❌ ④ discouraged(의욕이 꺾인): 원문은 motivated. 달력의 새로운 시작 효과로 더 의욕적으로 느꼈다는 맥락에서 discouraged는 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: motivated(동기부여된) ↔ discouraged(의욕이 꺾인). 본문 전체가 동기 부여 주제

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). questions.stem: 연구에서 날짜가 새로운 시작과 연관될 때 학생들은 그 시점을 목표 추구를 시작하기에 더 매력적인 시간으로 보았다.

det.korean: T(참): 날짜를 새로운 시작으로 제시할 때 목표 추구를 시작하기 더 좋은 시점으로 인식
det.analysis: ✅ T: 원문 'students viewed it as a more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit'와 일치
det.tip: kick-start = 시작하다. 새로운 시작 연관 날짜 → 더 매력적인 시작 시점으로 인식

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). questions.stem: 최근 연구에서 달력의 현재 날을 한 주의 마지막 날로 표시하자 목표 달성 동기가 높아졌다.

det.korean: F(거짓): 원문에서는 마지막 날이 아니라 첫 번째 날로 묘사할 때 동기가 높아짐
det.analysis: ❌ F: 원문은 'depicted the current day as the first day of the week'(한 주의 첫 번째 날로 묘사). '마지막 날'이 아니라 '첫 번째 날'로 표시해야 동기가 높아짐
det.tip: first(첫 번째) ≠ last(마지막). 새로운 시작 = first day = 동기 부여

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). Whether it was starting a new gym habit or spending less time on social media, when the date that researchers suggested was associated with a new beginning, more students wanted to begin changes right then. And more recent research by a different team found that similar benefits were achieved by showing goal seekers modified weekly calendars. When calendars depicted the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the first day of the week, people reported feeling more motivated to make immediate progress on their goals.
questions.stem: 달력 연구에서 현재 날을 한 주의 시작으로 보여주었을 때 사람들은 목표에 즉각적인 진전을 이루고자 하는 동기를 더 느꼈다.

det.korean: T(참): 달력에서 현재 날을 첫날로 묘사하면 목표에 즉각적인 진전 동기가 상승
det.analysis: ✅ T: 원문 'people reported feeling more motivated to make immediate progress on their goals'와 일치
det.tip: immediate progress = 즉각적인 진전. 달력이 현재 날을 첫날로 보여줄 때 동기 상승

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: unremarkable(평범한, 특별하지 않은)
det.analysis:
❌ ① meaningful(의미 있는): 새로운 시작과 대비되는 날이므로 의미 있는 날은 부적절
❌ ② exciting(신나는): 동기 유발 효과 없는 평범한 날과 반대 의미
✅ ③ unremarkable: 원문 일치. 새로운 시작(new beginning)과 대비되는 '평범하고 특별하지 않은' 날로 제시됨 ←정답
❌ ④ memorable(기억에 남는): 기억에 남는 날도 동기를 높일 수 있어 대비가 약함
det.tip: unremarkable(특별하지 않은) ↔ new beginning(새로운 시작). 두 조건을 대비해 동기 차이를 보임

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). Whether it was starting a new gym habit or spending less time on social media, when the date that researchers suggested was associated with a new beginning, more students wanted to begin changes right then. And more recent research by a different team found that similar benefits were achieved by showing goal seekers __________. When calendars depicted the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the first day of the week, people reported feeling more motivated to make immediate progress on their goals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: modified weekly calendars(수정된 주간 달력)
det.analysis:
❌ ① completed task lists(완료된 할 일 목록): 달력 수정과 무관한 내용
✅ ② modified weekly calendars: 원문 일치. 수정된 주간 달력을 보여줌으로써 유사한 혜택 달성 ←정답
❌ ③ annual goal reports(연간 목표 보고서): 연간 보고서 언급 없음
❌ ④ random date choices(무작위 날짜 선택): 무작위가 아닌 새로운 시작 날짜 활용
det.tip: modified weekly calendars → 현재 날을 첫날로 표시 → 새로운 시작 효과 → 동기 상승

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). Whether it was starting a new gym habit or spending less time on social media, when the date that researchers suggested was associated with a new beginning, more students wanted to begin changes right then. And more recent research by a different team found that similar benefits were achieved by showing goal seekers modified weekly calendars. When calendars depicted the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the first day of the week, people reported feeling more motivated to make immediate progress on their goals.
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 연구자들은 날짜가 목표 달성 여부와 무관하다고 주장했다.
날짜가 새로운 시작과 연관될 때 더 많은 학생들이 즉시 변화를 시작하길 원했다.
달력 연구는 첫 번째 연구팀이 진행한 후속 연구이다.
달력에서 현재 날을 한 주의 마지막 날로 표시하면 동기가 높아진다.

det.korean: 날짜가 새로운 시작과 연관될 때 더 많은 학생들이 즉시 변화를 시작하길 원했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① '날짜가 목표와 무관' — 본문 전체가 날짜와 목표 동기의 관계를 다룸
✅ ② '더 많은 학생들이 즉시 변화를 시작하길 원했다' — 원문 'more students wanted to begin changes right then'과 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ '첫 번째 연구팀의 후속 연구' — 원문은 'a different team'(다른 팀)
❌ ④ '마지막 날로 표시하면 동기 상승' — 원문은 first day(첫 번째 날)로 표시
det.tip: right then = 바로 그때/즉시. 새로운 시작 날짜 = 즉각적 행동 의지 증가

questions.passage: In one study, when researchers suggested that a date was associated with a new beginning (such as "the first day of spring"), students viewed it as a more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit than when researchers presented it as an unremarkable day (such as "the third Thursday in March"). Whether it was starting a new gym habit or spending less time on social media, when the date that researchers suggested was associated with a new beginning, more students wanted to begin changes right then. And more recent research by a different team found that similar benefits were achieved by showing goal seekers modified weekly calendars. When calendars depicted the current day (either Monday or Sunday) as the first day of the week, people reported feeling more motivated to make immediate progress on their goals.
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 날짜가 새로운 시작으로 여겨질 때 목표 추구 시작 시점으로 더 선호되었다.
달력 연구는 첫 번째 연구와 다른 팀이 진행했다.
달력 연구에서 목요일을 첫 번째 날로 설정하였다.
사람들은 달력에서 현재 날이 첫날로 표시될 때 즉각적인 진전 동기를 더 느꼈다.

det.korean: 목요일이 아니라 월요일(Monday) 또는 일요일(Sunday)을 첫날로 설정
det.analysis:
✅ ① '목표 추구 시작 시점으로 더 선호' — more attractive time to kick-start goal pursuit와 일치
✅ ② '다른 팀이 진행' — 'a different team'과 일치
❌ ③ '목요일을 첫 번째 날로' — 원문은 'either Monday or Sunday'(월요일 또는 일요일). 목요일은 오류 ←정답
